texts: good. the questioning is placed two days before the equinox as a measured gap rather than an invented date, and the Council, Coraline Ash and the Watch all land in the right slots on the event.

good. the duration attaches to the questioning event introduced in the previous sentence, so the two sentences share one event rather than splitting into two. One caveat that needs no rewrite: 'afternoon' is stored as the duration unit, and it is a day-part word rather than a convertible unit, so a later 'how many hours did it last?' question will not resolve against it.

bad: everything Old Vesh said is dropped — the parse records only that Vesh spoke — because a complement whose whole content is a negative determiner ('had no apprentice candidate') has no way to carry its polarity inside a reported claim, so the translator discards it, and 'that year' goes with it. Say the same thing with a positive verb: "Old Vesh said that the village lacked an apprentice candidate from a Keeper family that year." — 'lacked' is an ordinary positive predicate, so the whole report is kept and 'that year' can pick up Year 1 from the first sentence. Separately, consider writing the name as plain 'Vesh' wherever the epithet is not doing work: 'Old Vesh' can be read either as the whole name or as 'Old' plus the name, and the two readings give different symbols across episodes.

bad: 'as an apprentice' sits inside 'voted to accept …', which the translator must leave neutral about whether the accepting actually happened, so the apprentice role has nowhere licensed to go — the parse asserts it anyway, hanging an apprentice state and a caused-result link off an event the sentence only proposes; Coraline is also slotted as something the accepting changes rather than as the person chosen. Put the outcome in the main clause: "The Council accepted Coraline Ash as an apprentice by a vote." — the accepting is then stated outright, the apprentice role is a plain state holding of her, and the vote is kept as the means.

mixed: the assignment itself is right — Council assigning, Coraline assigned, Pell receiving, past tense — but 'as an apprentice' is recorded as a result the assigning caused, and it reuses the very apprentice-state the accepting event was given, so the parse claims one state was produced by two different events. State her standing separately instead: "The Council assigned the apprentice Coraline Ash to Pell." — being an apprentice is then a plain fact about her, with nothing claiming the assignment created it.
good. the age is kept as a past-tense measurement of Pell on the 'old' scale, nineteen years, which is exactly the licensed form.

bad: 'in the previous year' has no backward-shift rule to follow, so the parse invents the calendar term Year 0 by subtracting one from the equinox's Year 1 two sentences away, and the past perfect is left with nothing recording that the completion came before the vote and the assignment. Anchor it to a stated event: "Pell had completed an apprenticeship one year before the Council questioned Coraline Ash." — that yields a measured one-year gap against something the episode actually asserts instead of a made-up year number, and it carries the 'had' ordering explicitly.
